description: Eleventh-round conservative temporal backfill candidates for unresearched MENA/South Asia research_temporal_dates rows. This report is research-only and is not merged into temporal overrides.
scope_notes: Only rows with recommended_action=research_temporal_dates, prior_research_status=not_researched, and country_code in EG, SY, LY, SA, AE, DZ, IR, PK, IQ, BH, LB were considered.
Rows marked previously_candidate, previously_skipped_no_safe_date, prior_candidate, or prior_skipped were excluded.
Included source_ids were checked against webapp/static_public/data/map_overlays/military_base_temporal_overrides.json and were not present there at generation time.
Rows with only current gazetteer, map, prayer-time, tide, or airport-directory presence and no dated operational marker were placed in skipped[].
Where no public establishment date was found, start_year is a conservative documented-by operational year, not an inferred construction year.

candidates.name: King Faisal Naval Base

source_notes.title: GlobalSecurity.org - Royal Saudi Naval Forces, Western Fleet
source_notes.note: Western Fleet history states that King Faisal Naval Base officially opened in 1404 AH, corresponding to 1984 CE.

source_notes.title: Saudipedia - Royal Saudi Naval Forces
source_notes.note: Saudi reference article identifies King Faisal Naval Base in Jeddah as a Naval Forces school and Western Fleet location.

candidates.rationale: The queue row is the Jeddah naval-base feature. The official-opening evidence is Hijri-year based and machine-translated in the accessible source, so the Gregorian year is used with medium confidence.

candidates.name: Sarra Air Base

source_notes.title: Battle of Maaten al-Sarra
source_notes.note: Battle history identifies the 5 September 1987 raid against the Libyan Maaten al-Sarra Air Base.

source_notes.title: Maaten al-Sarra Air Base
source_notes.note: Base profile describes Maaten al-Sarra as the main southern Libyan air base in the final phase of the Chadian-Libyan conflict.

candidates.rationale: The GeoNames Sarra Air Base row aligns with Maaten al-Sarra Air Base. No opening year was found, so 1987 is a documented-by wartime operational year rather than a construction date.

candidates.name: Kahlid Army

source_notes.title: Dawn - Terrorists on the run after Zarb-i-Azb operation, says COAS
source_notes.note: 2014 ISPR-linked coverage names Khalid Army Aviation Base Quetta and reports that Army Aviation assets remained safe after an attempted attack.

source_notes.title: Mapcarta - Kahlid Army
source_notes.note: Gazetteer page links the GeoNames feature to Kahlid Army near Quetta and lists alternate names Quetta Airfield and Quetta Heliport.

candidates.rationale: The queue spelling appears to be a GeoNames variant for Khalid Army Aviation Base at Quetta. The 2014 start is only a documented-by operational/security incident year, so confidence is low.

candidates.name: Omidiyeh

source_notes.title: Omidiyeh Air Base
source_notes.note: Air-base profile identifies Omidiyeh as an Iranian military air base and cites DAFIF data current as of October 2006.

source_notes.title: GlobalSecurity.org - Umidiyeh Air Base
source_notes.note: Facility profile identifies the site as the 5th Tactical Air Base outside Umidiyeh/Omidiyeh in southwestern Iran.

candidates.rationale: No establishment date was found. The 2006 start is a conservative documented-by operational year from DAFIF-linked military-airport data.

candidates.name: Hamah

source_notes.title: Hama Air Base
source_notes.note: Air-base profile identifies Hama Military Airport as a Syrian military airbase and cites DAFIF data effective October 2006.

source_notes.title: Small Wars Journal - Suheil al-Hassan and the Syrian Army's Tiger Forces
source_notes.note: 2016 military analysis describes Syrian aircraft and other military assets at Hama Airbase by the end of 2012.

candidates.rationale: The queue row is the GeoNames short form for Hama Air Base. No opening year was found, so 2006 is a dated military-airport directory marker, supported by later operational use.

candidates.name: Tall Afar

source_notes.title: Mapcarta - Tall Afar
source_notes.note: Gazetteer summary describes Tal Afar Air Base as constructed in 1983 for the Iraqi Air Force and operated until the 2003 invasion.

source_notes.title: Tall Afar Air Base - Military Wiki
source_notes.note: Facility history describes Tall Afar as a former Iraqi Air Force base captured by Coalition forces during Operation Iraqi Freedom in 2003.

candidates.rationale: The GeoNames row maps to Tal/Tall Afar Air Base. The 1983 construction and 2003 Iraqi Air Force endpoint are clear in secondary facility histories, though not official Iraqi records.

candidates.name: Um Almelh

source_notes.title: Umm Al Melh Border Guards Airport
source_notes.note: Facility history states the air base was commissioned by the Ministry of Interior in November 2010 for Border Guards southern-border operations.

source_notes.title: Mapcarta - Um Almelh
source_notes.note: Gazetteer page links the GeoNames row to Umm Al Melh Border Guards Airport and repeats the November 2010 commissioning history.

candidates.rationale: The row is the GeoNames Um Almelh airbase feature, and the linked Border Guards Airport history gives a direct commissioned year.

candidates.name: Fort Suse

source_notes.title: Fort Suse
source_notes.note: Facility history says Fort Suse was built in 1977 by Russian engineers as a barracks and training facility, converted in 2005, and handed over in September 2006.

source_notes.title: Global Policy Forum - Iraq: a decade of abuses
source_notes.note: Detention report describes Fort Suse as a former Iraqi military barracks near Sulaymaniyah, reconstructed and opened in 2005, then handed to Iraqi authorities in September 2006.

candidates.rationale: The queue row is a barracks feature. The start uses the 1977 barracks/training-facility construction date; the end marks the 2006 handover from coalition military detention use to Iraqi authority, not demolition of the physical site.

candidates.name: Al Minhad Air Base

source_notes.title: Camp Mirage
source_notes.note: Camp Mirage history says the facility was established in late December 2001 and was widely reported to be located at Al Minhad Air Base.

source_notes.title: Nautilus Institute - Al Minhad Air Base
source_notes.note: Australian basing analysis reports that by late 2009 Australian operations in the Gulf, Iraq, and Afghanistan were based from Al Minhad.

candidates.rationale: No public UAE Air Force opening year was found. The 2001 start is a documented-by coalition logistics presence at Al Minhad, so confidence is low for the base's true opening date.

candidates.name: Oum el Bouaghi Airport

source_notes.title: Algerian Air Forces - Chief of Staff visit to Oum El Bouaghi Air Base
source_notes.note: Official Algerian Air Forces notice records a 7 September 2023 working and inspection visit to Oum El Bouaghi Air Base in the 5th Military Region.

source_notes.title: Oum El Bouaghi Air Base - Airprt.net
source_notes.note: Airport profile identifies QMH/DABO as Oum El Bouaghi Air Base near Oum El Bouaghi city.

candidates.rationale: No establishment date was found. The official 2023 Algerian military visit is a dated operational marker for the named air base, not an opening year.

candidates.name: ISA Air Base

source_notes.title: Air & Space Power Journal - Origins of the Royal Bahraini Air Force
source_notes.note: Air University article states that Bahrain's F-16s arrived in 1990 and Shaikh Isa Air Base opened in southern Bahrain.

source_notes.title: Isa Air Base
source_notes.note: Base profile identifies Isa Air Base, formerly Shaikh Isa Air Base, as a Royal Bahraini Air Force military installation.

candidates.rationale: The queue row maps directly to Isa/Shaikh Isa Air Base, and the Air University source gives an explicit opening year.

candidates.name: Beirut Air Base

source_notes.title: Beirut Air Base
source_notes.note: Base history states that Beirut Air Base was established in 1950 after formation of the Lebanese Air Force.

source_notes.title: ICAO - Lebanon's Action Plan 2023
source_notes.note: Lebanon civil aviation action plan notes that Beirut airport also houses Beirut Air Base, the main base for the Lebanese Air Force.

candidates.rationale: The row directly names Beirut Air Base. The 1950 establishment date is available in a base history, with an official aviation plan supporting the current facility identity.
